# fix(upflow): instrument the ADO half, and guard the one unguarded host

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.

**Commit**: `403fa30102e2` — fix(upflow): instrument the ADO half, and guard the one unguarded host

**Body**:

Round 5 of the adversarial redteam. Three lanes, all NOT-CLEAN; no live code
defect, but the ADO lane turned out to be fixed-at-both-surfaces and
instrumented-at-one — the same shape Round 4 already named about itself.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Restoring the caller-authored `cwd` seam in the ADO
adapter redded NOTHING. Driven directly under that mutation the adapter
returned ok:true, fired:true and MERGED ON THE UPSTREAM while all 36 fixtures
stayed green. CRIT-2 was fixed at both adapters and guarded at one; GitHub
carries the case labelled "regression guard for the originating CRIT" and ADO
had no sibling. `ado/descriptor-identity-seams-are-ignored` is that sibling —
measured to red exactly one case (itself) under the seam mutation.

The `_parseAdo` exact-count PAIR had zero instrument AND the source asserted
otherwise: the comment called the pair "how the originating exploit was
actually closed", which reads as a claim it was tested. Measured, the pair
redded nothing and was VACUOUS, not inert. No existing ADO case could cover it
— every one carries a DIRTY segment that validate-before-drop catches before
the count gates are reached, so the gap needed an ALL-CLEAN multi-segment
remote, which nothing drove. Added, and the false claim is recorded rather than
quietly replaced.

The host was the ONE identity operand with no ASCII precheck, while
`normalizeComponent` guards the components it is compared alongside. Not a live
bypass — no current host-set member contains a "k", and U+212A is the only code
point that lowercases into ASCII usefully. Closed anyway because this file's own
standard is that safe-by-accident becomes a bypass the moment a caller compares
hosts differently, and vcs-github-adapter.js explicitly schedules exactly that
change ("A GHES deployment adds its appliance host here").

Also: `_lastGitStderr` was never cleared, so a refusal could quote git stderr
from an unrelated earlier call as though git had said it on this one; and
`PROVIDERS[id]` was a prototype-chain lookup, so getProvider("constructor")
returned ok.

Mutation-validated in an isolated sandbox; the working tree was never mutated.
Each new case reds exactly itself; each count gate alone remains inert and the
pair reds, so the comment's arithmetic is measured, not argued.
